text:
alex: FYI ran a 2-hour perf pass on qwen2.5 serving config, found a regression vs last week after the kernel-picker change. attaching quick profiler snapshot below. :grimacing:

mira: ugh, which kernel change? the heuristics that prefer split-gemm on A100?

alex: yes. the picker now prefers kernel_v2 for layers with seq_len>512. that reduced p99 on long-context but increased median for 2048 workloads. profiler: 
```
model: qwen2.5-medium
batch: 8
seq: 1024
median_tok_ms: 5.6 -> 6.9 (+23%)
p99_tok_ms: 32.1 -> 18.7 (-42%)
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.78
avg_gpu_util: 63% -> 71%
```

jon: interesting. so wins at tail but worse median. any change in batching patterns?

alex: batching more aggressive because picker increased throughput per-instance; autoscaler pushed more concurrent requests which made average effective batch size jump from 3.1 -> 5.4. that amplifies latency median.

sasha: Did you correlate with kv-cache behavior? I've seen cases where kv cache warms slower and then batching overfills and we spin up kernels suboptimally.

alex: checked that. kv cache warmup for chat-like sessions dropped by ~18% in hit rate for qwen2.5 tokenizers for multi-ling prompts. suspect tokenizer edge cases produce slightly different tokenization boundaries, causing earlier cache misses and more repeated prefix work.

mira: multi-ling tokenizer edgecases? like CJK + emoji + whitespace normalization? any reproducible example?

alex: repro: Chinese prompt with interspersed ASCII code snippets + zero-width joiner emoji. tokenizer splits into extra small tokens in our tokenizer patch (v3.2) which we rolled Monday. simple example: 
```
input: "你好, check this: 👩‍💻 code sample"
tokens(old): [你好, ,, check,  this, :,  👩, ‍, 💻,  code, sample]
tokens(new): [你, 好, ,, check, this, :,  👩‍💻, code, sample]
```
So new behavior reduces token count but shifts prefix boundaries -> mismatches to cached key/values because the model sees different token IDs for earlier positions. cache key derivation uses token offsets so mismatch.

jon: that explains kv miss spikes. If tokenization reduces tokens, offsets drift and cache lookup fails. we should make cache key independent of tokenizer id boundaries or include normalized text fingerprint.

sasha: alternatively, we can add a conservative compatibility layer: keep an alternate cache namespace keyed by model+tokenizer_version fingerprint for a while, and fall back to full recompute if mismatch.

perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: qwen2.5 median latency increase detected on serving-prod cluster us-west-2 between 1768420000 and 1768456000. CI tag: kernel-picker-v2. Rolled back on canary at 1768454000? false, rollout completed.

mira: thanks bot. idea: tweak kernel-picker scoring to include expected effective batch size and kv_cache_hit_rate weight. currently score = throughput_score * kernel_speed_factor. we should add penalty for reduced cache affinity and for larger avg_batch_size causing queueing.

alex: proposed quick patch: score = throughput_score * kernel_speed_factor - alpha * (1 - kv_hit_rate) - beta * max(0, avg_batch_size - target_bs). using alpha=0.6,beta=0.12 gave simulated median improvement ~10% in our offline model.

jon: also worth checking attention head vs kv_head dims. I instrumented a few qwen2.5 variants and saw head_count != kv_head_count in some conversions from HF weights -> runtime config. that produced hidden API mismatches and suboptimal kernel selection fallback. snippet from conversion log: 
```
INFO: layer 17: attn_heads=32, kv_heads=16 -> forcing kv-reshape path -> slower matmuls
```
we should error on mismatch during model load rather than silently fallback.

sasha: agree. silent fallback hides perf cliffs. raise a strict warning and default to a safe reshape only under a flag. we can also add an offline converter fix to align kv dims where possible.

alex: another angle: rope scaling strategies. qwen2.5 uses RoPE with scaled frequency for long-context. we tried linear scaling and ALiBi overlay in a hybrid. ALiBi helped p99 but made short context perplexity slightly worse and seems to interact with kernel_v2's pos-encoding fused kernels. Some kernels assume standard RoPE layout, others accept ALiBi deltas. mismatch triggers slow generic path.

mira: can we tag kernels with supported_pos_enc={rope,scaled_rope,alibi,rope+alibi} and have the picker prefer exact matches? that would avoid choosing a kernel that falls back to generic.

alex: yes, implemented proof-of-concept. picker now filters by supported_pos_enc subset before scoring. on sims, median improved back and p99 maintained. downside: reduces kernel pool for some variants so throughput might drop.

perf-bot: note: adding compatibility filter reduced available kernels by 18% on a100-small nodes. autoscaler triggered scale-up in 3 clusters.

jon: then add fallback policy: prefer exact pos_enc match, if unavailable and kv_hit_rate high then pick close match, else fall back to current behavior. also add a threshold on batch_size to avoid picking high-throughput kernels when queueing is small.

sasha: about tokenizer: let's add a tokenization-version header in the request context so cache namespaces are explicit. short-term fix. long-term: make cache keys be based on normalized string fingerprint + model_version, not token offsets.

alex: agreed. I'll push two PRs: 1) picker scoring tweaks + pos-enc filter + strict model-load check for head/kv mismatches. 2) request header for tokenizer_version + migration of cache namespace.

mira: can you also add a small perf test in our e2e harness for mixed CJK+emoji inputs and measure kv-hit curves? want to avoid regressions from tokenizer changes.

alex: yes, test case added locally. will submit draft PRs in next 2 hours. tagging @sasha for review on cache migration plan.

sasha: ack. will prioritize. also queue an infra note: if picker filter reduces kernel pool below 70% capacity, we should auto-enable a temp quota to avoid scale-up cost. @infra-bot ping? :eyes:

infra-bot: noted. created ticket INF-3124 to evaluate temporary quota gating when kernel-pool-availability < 0.7. linking to thread.

jon: cool. summary: short-term: token-version header and picker scoring tweak. medium: pos-enc kernel tags + strict load validation. long-term: normalize cache keys and fix tokenizer conversion drift. thanks alex for the triage. :party_parrot:
